scope.description: Whole xarray labelled-array and dataset functionality across data preparation, analysis and interchange.
scope.denominator: Labelled arrays and datasets, indexing and selection, named-dimension arithmetic and reduction, alignment and merging, grouping/resampling/rolling, coordinate and calendar handling, storage backends, lazy/distributed execution and scientific inspection.

coverage.rationale: One classic-NetCDF variable can be selected by named numeric coordinate ranges and reduced to an unweighted mean profile. Most labelled-array operations, dataset combinations, scientific metadata conventions and storage/execution backends remain outside this integration; a coarse 5% whole-application estimate reflects that narrow breadth.

scope.description: Bounded local classic-NetCDF measurement-cube selection into a one-axis unweighted mean profile with declared variable, layout/unit assertions, coordinate ranges, missing-data policy and numeric plotting handoff.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within this one-variable profile workflow; general xarray analysis and excluded scientific conventions are outside this denominator.

abstraction.rationale: Authors declare coordinates, selection, retained dimension and missingness rather than write array code or native serialization. Independent finite-array checks and a typed profile publication support reuse, but users still supply storage-order and unit assertions, choose the missing policy and arrange scientifically appropriate weighting or plotting outside the supported slice.

limitations: One bounded CDF-1 classic-NetCDF cube and one variable with strictly increasing numeric coordinates; selected retained profiles have at most 2048 points. No general CF/calendar, packed values, NetCDF4/HDF5, Zarr, remote or Dask workflow.

The reduction is an unweighted mean with explicit skip, propagate or refuse policy and conditioning refusal. No inferred units, alignment, interpolation, measurement uncertainty or scientific-validity certification.

Dimension-list order is a deliberate storage-layout assertion, although reduction uses named dimensions. A plotting consumer has its own row, finite-value, header and unit contract; artifact kind alone does not establish compatibility.
Subjective source-contract estimates rounded to five points, not exhaustive API measurements. Native runtime availability and source-bound qualification remain separate facts.
